fields.h1: Build a Logo Design Questionnaire Clients Finish Before Sketching
fields.hero_description: Build a logo design questionnaire that turns each client's answers into a brief your designer can sketch from.
fields.features_heading: What a Designer Needs Before the First Sketch
fields.features_subheading: Words like modern or clean mean something different from every client. These six pieces ask for answers a designer can draw from.
fields.feature_1:
The name exactly as it should read

Ask for the business name with its spelling and capitals, any tagline, and whether the full name or an initial should lead. A misspelling caught here costs nothing to fix.
fields.feature_2:
A list of where the logo will appear

Clients tick each place the logo goes: signs, packaging, profile photos, stickers, or shirts. Each tick adds the file it needs to the brief, like a square icon for a profile photo.
fields.feature_3:
Sample logos to vote on

Show a set of sample logos and ask for a thumbs up or down on each, with a reason required for every down vote. A client who cannot name a style can still point at the one they want.
fields.feature_4:
Current files sent with the answers

Clients upload the logo they use today, any brand fonts and photos of the storefront. Ask for an SVG if one exists, because an SVG renders at any size without loss of quality.
fields.feature_5:
A brief in the designer's inbox

Each response saves to a database you own, and the app emails the designer a brief with the answers grouped by section. Answers from several people on one project share a record.
fields.feature_6:
The questionnaire's code, yours to move

On paid plans, export the full codebase to your GitHub repository and host it beside your portfolio. Emergent built it from a prompt, and any change after that is one more prompt.

fields.usecase_heading: Logo Projects That Start From the Answers
fields.tab_content_1:
A sticker and a profile photo add a square icon

Gethin Moxley designs logos for new businesses. Tansy Ferreby, who is opening Cinderford Bakery, ticks where her logo will appear, including a 1-inch round sticker and the Instagram profile photo. Either one adds a square icon to the brief, so Gethin's brief for Tansy lists 2 files: the full logo and the square icon.
fields.tab_content_2:
Yes to three wordmarks, no to both mascots

Wickersham Studio sends Heathcote Dental 8 sample logos to vote on. Ksenia Cadwell, the office manager, likes 3 of them, all wordmarks, and votes down the other 5. Her reason on both mascots is the same: looks like a kids' brand. The designer opens the project to that tally, and the first sketches are lettering only.
fields.tab_content_3:
With two inks on the order, the logo gets two colors

Starling Print Co. designs logos for the businesses that order its shirts. Glenrock Landscaping orders 40 screen-printed shirts in 2 ink colors from a phone. The shop's rule is that a logo uses no more colors than the order prints, so the brief says to draw it in 2: forest green and white.
fields.tab_content_4:
Each board member answers, and the color vote splits

All 5 board members at Bramhope Youth Soccer answer the questionnaire on their own. Four of the 5 pick a crest, but the color vote splits, with 3 for green and 2 for navy. Esme Wilmer, the designer, gets an email naming the split and asks the board to settle the color before she sketches.

fields.howto_title: How to Build a Logo Design Questionnaire
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to write a logo design questionnaire that hands your designer a brief they can use, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Start from the brief you want back
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Ask who the logo is for
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 List every place the logo will live
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down the brief your designer wants on day one: the name, the files, the colors, the style, and the deadline. Every question on the form should fill one line of that brief. A question that fills none of them comes off the form.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask what the business does in one sentence and who buys from it. A bakery that sells to families and one that sells wedding cakes need different marks. Keep these as short text answers so the client writes in their own words.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Give the client a checklist of places such as signs, packaging, the website, vehicles, and shirts. Ask for the size wherever the space is small, like a sticker or an app icon. The deliverables are then settled before you send the quote.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Pick 8 sample logos in different styles and ask for a vote on each. Require a reason on every down vote. The reasons tell you more than the votes, and they pin down what a client means by a word like modern.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Ask for the current logo, brand fonts, and any colors the client must keep, such as a parent company's palette. Request an SVG where one exists. Mark these questions optional, because a business that is just opening may have none of it.
fields.howto_step_6_des: When several people sign off, such as partners or a board, send each one the questionnaire and group their answers under one project. Have the app email you when their answers disagree, and settle the difference before the first sketch.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Describe it to Emergent and test it
fields.howto_step_7_des: Paste your questions into a prompt, and Emergent turns them into the questionnaire and its database. Fill it in once the way a client would, read the brief that arrives, and change any question with one more prompt before you send the link.
fields.hero_prompt: Build a logo design questionnaire that saves every response to a database I own.

faq_plan.q: What is a logo design questionnaire?
faq_plan.a: A logo design questionnaire is the set of questions a client answers before a designer starts on their logo. It asks what the business does, who it serves, where the logo will appear, which styles the client likes, and when it is due. The answers become the designer's brief.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a logo design questionnaire?
faq_plan.a: List what your designer needs to know before sketching, then write one question for each item. Describe those questions to Emergent's AI form builder in plain English, and it builds the questionnaire with a database behind it. Fill it in yourself once before any client sees it.

faq_plan.q: What should I change in a logo design questionnaire template before using it?
faq_plan.a: Cut a logo design questionnaire template down to the work you take on. If you only design logos, strip out questions that belong to other jobs, such as website pages or print quantities. Then add the questions your last few clients made you ask by email.

faq_plan.q: How much brand strategy should a logo design questionnaire cover?
faq_plan.a: Only enough to draw from: what the business does, who buys from it, and a few words for how it should feel. Positioning, voice, and competitor research belong in a separate brand questionnaire, which a client needing a full identity answers before the logo work starts.

faq_plan.q: How many questions should a logo design questionnaire have?
faq_plan.a: Keep it near 20, grouped into short sections a client can finish in one sitting. Drop any question whose answer would not change a sketch or a file in the brief. Put optional questions, like uploads of current files, at the end.

faq_plan.q: When should a client fill out the logo design questionnaire?
faq_plan.a: After they agree to work with you and before the first sketch. Send it before the quote instead if the answers set the price, such as the number of logo files. Emergent puts no cap on responses, so one questionnaire link can stay open for every new client.

faq_plan.q: What happens after a client submits a logo design questionnaire?
faq_plan.a: The answers become your brief. Read them within a day and send back anything skipped or vague before you sketch. Billing contacts and account access belong in a client onboarding questionnaire, so the logo brief stays about design. An app built with Emergent can email you the brief as soon as a client submits.

faq_plan.q: Can a logo design questionnaire collect the client's current logo files?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Add an upload question for the current logo, brand fonts, and photos of where the logo appears today. Check how your form tool handles uploads first: in Google Forms, responders need to sign in to a Google Account to answer a file upload question.

faq_plan.q: Should a logo design questionnaire be an online form or a fillable document?
faq_plan.a: An online form. A logo design questionnaire pdf has to be filled in, saved, and emailed back, and then you copy its answers into your brief by hand. An online form saves each answer when the client submits, and an app built with Emergent keeps every response in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: Should revision rounds and fees go in the logo design questionnaire?
faq_plan.a: No. Put the number of revision rounds, the fee, and the payment dates in the agreement the client signs, and keep the questionnaire to the brief. The same split works for any creative job, like keeping the shot list in a questionnaire and the terms in a wedding photography contract.

plan.angle: The top 10 is designer blog posts and printable question lists (Una Healy, Vistaprint, Lee Media, a Scribd file, a Reddit thread) that stop at the questions. This page shows what four kinds of logo work do with the answers: a usage checklist that sets which logo files the brief lists, sample logos the client rates so style is shown instead of described, a print order whose ink count sets the palette, and a board whose separate answers expose a split before the first sketch.
